substantive_proof_moves.text: If j is smaller than k, both endpoints keep their original time. Otherwise both endpoints are mapped to τ, and the increment is zero. The inequality on the right endpoint includes a fine cell that ends exactly at τ.

overall: The source describes a dependency chain from deterministic dyadic identities, scalar/vector Brownian moment estimates and L2 completion, through row quadratic variation, compact Taylor limits, linear/Hessian limits, terminal sphere Ito, and weak expected evolution. Different nodes have intentionally different horizons, measurability scopes, regularity and convergence modes. No source-fidelity judgment made at this stage.
